tests.test: Fault lines: fragility predicts progression lost when a player goes off
tests.note: Each pair: same match, same first hour, player removed at 60'. Outcome: progressive passes 60-95' lost.
tests.what_it_shows: The measure finds structurally important players in a passing system with no planted answer. Real football adds tactics, substitutes and opponents adapting: needs the injury/red-card study.

tests.note: Predictor and outcome centred by position, so 'midfielders matter more' does not count.

tests.test: Fault lines: better than counting passes
tests.bar: 95% CI of rho(fragility) - rho(passes) not below 0
tests.result: fragility -0.083 vs passes -0.109 vs betweenness -0.069 (difference CI -0.011 to 0.066)
tests.note: If a plain pass count predicts as well, fragility's extra complexity is not earning its place.

tests.test: Plan fit: robust to the exact weights
tests.note: Every weight multiplied by a random 0.5-1.5. A low tau would mean the ranking is mostly my weight choices.
tests.what_it_shows: Holds for any data: this is a property of the scoring, not of football.

tests.test: Plan fit: early reads hold up
tests.bar: same side of 50 as the 90' read: 30' >= 65%, 45' >= 75%
tests.note: Checks that the minutes adjustment keeps early verdicts from flipping later.
tests.what_it_shows: Real players vary more between halves (tactics, fatigue, game state), so expect lower agreement on real data.

tests.test: Plan fit: reliable within a match
tests.note: A score that changes completely between halves is measuring noise, not the player.
tests.what_it_shows: In synthetic matches players have no lasting individual quality beyond position and team strength, so this is a floor; real players should be more consistent.

tests.test: Flags: not too many, not too few
tests.bar: 0.2-2.5 alert flags per team per check
tests.note: Too many flags and coaches stop reading them.
tests.what_it_shows: Rates will shift on real data; retune the 1.5x / 0.6x / 12-point thresholds there.

tests.bar: 95% CI of the fading effect below 0, controlling for the current 15-minute fit
tests.result: neutral: 1.7 (CI 0.01 to 3.75, 118 flags); storyline: -1.64 (CI -2.88 to -0.36, 133 flags)
tests.note: Next-15 fit regressed on current fit + the flag. Without the flag adding information, it is regression to the mean dressed up as insight.
tests.what_it_shows: The generator has no fatigue, so in neutral matches nothing real can fade; the storyline match (man-marking from 60') is the only true decline. Real test: tracking data (high-speed running) and coach substitutions.

tests.bar: median 2-10 non-goal cues per match, none above 20
tests.note: Counts fault-line shifts, alerts and narrowing per match.
tests.what_it_shows: Precision (are they the moments an analyst would pick?) needs analyst labels on real matches.

tests.note: Run 1 finding: xPA weights chances by what a goal is worth then, so a trailing team's chances count more and the margin does not track who won. It measures decisive moments, not dominance: use the xG margin for dominance.
tests.what_it_shows: By construction it inherits xG quality; on real data use the provider's xG.

tests.test: Expected points added beats old clutch points (added after run 1)
tests.bar: rho(xPA, realised points added) > rho(old clutch points, realised)
tests.result: xPA 0.60 vs clutch points -0.02 over 5280 player-matches
tests.note: Realised points added = goals (scorer and assister) x the points a goal was worth at that moment.
tests.what_it_shows: In synthetic data xG is the true scoring probability, which favours xPA; real xG is an estimate.

tests.note: Negations, opponent instructions, sheets, other languages, emphasis.
tests.what_it_shows: Language understanding: independent of the match data.
